living_cost.basis: Budget = official blocked-account monthly release (992 EUR, 11,904 EUR/year) set by the Federal Foreign Office. Moderate and comfortable are ESTIMATES taken from TUM's published Munich single-person range of approx. 1,300-2,000 EUR/month (Munich is Germany's most expensive student city; Saarland University quotes about 800 EUR/month for Saarbruecken).

student_visa.name: National visa (D visa) for study, section 16b Residence Act

fees.label: National visa fee, adult (charged in INR: INR 8,300 from 1 Oct 2026, from 30 Sep 2026 at VFS; the mission warns it can change at short notice with exchange rates)

proof_of_funds.text: Blocked account holding currently 11,904 EUR for the first year of studies; no more than 992 EUR can be withdrawn per month. Alternatives: formal obligation letter from a sponsor in Germany, German/EU public scholarship, or education loan. Applications go through the Consular Services Portal; Indian degree holders almost always need an APS certificate.

work_during_study.text: Up to 140 working days per year (working-day account). A day of up to 4 hours can count as a half day; in lecture periods weeks of up to 20 hours count as 2.5 days. Student assistant jobs (studentische Nebentaetigkeiten) at the university do not count toward the limit. No self-employment.

post_study_work.name: Residence permit for job seeking after graduation (section 20 Residence Act)
post_study_work.text: After successfully completing studies in Germany, graduates can get a residence permit for up to 18 months to look for a job matching their qualification, provided livelihood is secured. BAMF: any form of work may be taken up during this time. No employer sponsor needed.

pr_pathway.text: Settlement permit (permanent residence): German university graduates after 2 years on a skilled-worker/Blue Card residence title with a current job, 24 months of pension contributions and sufficient German. EU Blue Card holders after 27 months (21 months with sufficient German, B1). Other skilled workers: 3 years and 36 months contributions. 2026 Blue Card minimum salary: 50,700 EUR, or 45,934.20 EUR for shortage occupations and graduates within 3 years of degree (section 18g(2)).

recent_changes.title: EU Blue Card minimum salaries for 2026: 50,700 EUR standard, 45,934.20 EUR reduced
recent_changes.who_affected: Graduates and skilled workers applying for an EU Blue Card in 2026
recent_changes.impact: The reduced 45,934.20 EUR threshold applies to recent graduates (degree within 3 years) and shortage occupations such as IT, so a typical entry CS/DS salary in Germany clears it. Thresholds are indexed to the pension ceiling and rise every year.

check.note: The salary thresholds were confirmed only through secondary sources; the official Bundesanzeiger PDF could not be read.

recent_changes.title: TUM raises non-EU tuition from winter semester 2027/28
recent_changes.who_affected: Non-EU students starting at TUM in winter semester 2027/28 or later
recent_changes.impact: Master's tuition rises from 4,000/6,000 EUR to 4,600/6,800 EUR per semester. An Indian student starting a 6,000-EUR programme in 2027 could pay about 3,200 EUR more over 4 semesters. Students already enrolled keep their starting rate.

check.note: The page does not say which tier (4,600 or 6,800 EUR) a given programme moves to, so the 3,200 EUR estimate is an assumption.

recent_changes.title: German missions in India set national visa fee at INR 8,300
recent_changes.who_affected: All adult national (D) visa applicants in India
recent_changes.impact: Fee fixed in rupees (about 75 EUR); VFS applies it from 30 Sep 2026. Negligible ROI effect; VFS adds its own service fee.

recent_changes.title: Abolition of 3-year fast-track ('turbo') naturalisation
recent_changes.who_affected: Skilled migrants hoping for German citizenship after 3 years
recent_changes.impact: Citizenship now generally needs at least 5 years' residence. Does not affect study, job-search permit or PR timelines, but lengthens the path to an EU passport.

check.note: The cited source is a parliamentary speech, not the law; the effective date is not stated and the claim could not be confirmed.

recent_changes.title: Work-and-Stay-Agentur: single digital platform for skilled-worker immigration
recent_changes.who_affected: Foreign skilled workers and trainees; students not explicitly mentioned
recent_changes.impact: Cabinet adopted key points only; no launch date. Could speed up visa and recognition processing later, but no effect yet.

recent_changes.title: Skilled Immigration Act stage 2: more flexible student employment rules
recent_changes.impact: Students may hold side jobs under more flexible rules; current law allows 140 working days per year. Helps cover part of living costs during study.

recent_changes.title: Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte) introduced (Skilled Immigration Act stage 3)
recent_changes.who_affected: Job seekers from abroad (not graduates of German universities, who use the 18-month permit)
recent_changes.impact: Points-based 1-year job-search card. A fallback route; German graduates have the stronger 18-month permit.

check.note: The cited government page returned an error on 22 Oct 2026 and could not be re-checked.

policy_volatility.evidence: Core student-visa rules (blocked account 11,904 EUR, 140-day work rule, 18-month job-search permit) have been stable since 2024; changes in the last 24 months were mostly liberalising (Skilled Immigration Act 2024) plus the 2025 abolition of 3-year naturalisation and routine annual Blue Card indexation.

psw_uncertainty.evidence: Statutory 18-month job-search permit after graduation with no sponsor and any work allowed; a reduced Blue Card threshold (45,934.20 EUR in 2026) for recent graduates makes conversion to work status predictable.

work_restrictions.evidence: 140 full days per year during study (student assistant jobs exempt), unrestricted work during the 18-month job search. Many non-tech and business jobs still expect German, which limits practical options.

funds_burden.evidence: 11,904 EUR (about one year of living costs) must be locked up front in a blocked account before the visa; at public universities this is the largest upfront cost, though it is released monthly for living expenses.

recent_adverse.evidence: In the last 12 months: no adverse change to student visa or post-study rules; negatives are institutional (TUM tuition rise from WS 2027/28) and citizenship (5-year minimum after turbo naturalisation was abolished).

Low = median for under-25s (4,157 EUR); mid = lower quartile all ages (5,034 EUR); high = median all ages (6,301 EUR, all experience levels, so above true entry). Read via entgeltatlas-online.de (third-party mirror of BA data) because the official Entgeltatlas app/API could not be loaded.

tax.basis: ESTIMATE, not independently re-verified on 22 Oct 2026 (the OECD PDF could not be read). OECD Taxing Wages 2026: employee net average tax rate (income tax + employee social security contributions) for a single worker without children at the average wage in Germany was 38.7% in 2025. Entry salaries (about 50-65k EUR) sit below the OECD average wage, so the true rate is likely somewhat lower; 38.7% is a conservative figure. Tax class I, no church tax assumed.

checklist: Shortlist English-taught programmes and check intake deadlines (often 31 May / 15 May for winter intake).
Apply for the APS certificate early: Indian degree holders almost always need it for the visa and many universities.
Get IELTS/TOEFL (C1 often required; some universities reject medium-of-instruction letters); GMAT/GRE only for MBAs.
Apply directly or via uni-assist as each programme specifies; prepare SOP, CV, transcripts and references.
After admission, open a blocked account and deposit 11,904 EUR (992 EUR/month release).
Buy health insurance valid from your arrival date (statutory or private, as accepted by the mission).
Submit the national (D) student visa application via the Consular Services Portal and book the VFS appointment; fee INR 8,300.
On arrival: register your address (Anmeldung), enrol, pay the semester fee and open a German bank account.
Apply to the local Auslaenderbehoerde for the residence permit before the entry visa expires.
Start learning German (B1 helps for jobs and shortens Blue Card PR from 27 to 21 months); plan the 18-month job-search permit before your permit expires.
